{{Short description|Japanese Mathematician}}
'''Hayato Chiba''' (千葉 逸人, born 18 January 1982) is a Japanese mathematician and professor at the Advanced Institute for Materials Research of [[Tōhoku University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.wpi-aimr.tohoku.ac.jp/chiba/|title = 千葉逸人|publisher = www.wpi-aimr.tohoku.ac.jp|date = |accessdate = 2019-06-14|archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20190614070501/https://www.wpi-aimr.tohoku.ac.jp/chiba/|archivedate = 2019-06-14}}</ref> He mainly concerns himself with the theory of dynamical systems, especially [[bifurcation theory]], and proved the [[Kuramoto Model|Kuramoto conjecture]] about infinite-dimensional differential equations with [[chaos theory|chaotic]] behavior.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Chiba |first=Hayato |date=2 August 2010 |title=A proof of the Kuramoto conjecture for a bifurcation structure of the infinite dimensional Kuramoto model |url=http://arxiv.org/abs/1008.0249 |journal=Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems |volume=35 |issue=3 |pages=762–834 |doi=10.1017/etds.2013.68 |issn=0143-3857|arxiv=1008.0249 }}</ref> He obtained his doctorate degree in information sciences at the [[University of Kyoto]].

== Education and Work ==
Chiba studied at [[Kyōto University | Kyōto University's]] engineering department, where he graduated in 2005. He continued on to pursue a doctorate degree, studying mainly analytic mechanics and non-linear differential equations until 2009, also at the University of Kyōto.

In the third year of his undergraduate studies, Chiba published a textbook on mathematical methods in engineering with Pleiades Publishing.<ref>{{Cite web |title=数学者への道のり |url=https://www.t.kyoto-u.ac.jp/publicity/no64/introduction/chiba |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=京都大学 工学広報 |language=ja}}</ref> A textbook about analytic geometry soon followed.

Starting from 2013, he worked at [[Kyūshū University]]'s research institute Mathematics for Industry as an untenured professor.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www2.math.kyushu-u.ac.jp/~chiba/ |title=Hayato Chiba |access-date=2022-11-22 |archive-date=2018-02-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180213023202/http://www2.math.kyushu-u.ac.jp/~chiba/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> During this time, he finalised and submitted his proof for the Kuramoto conjecture, which was then published in [[Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems]] in 2015.

2017, he appeared in a pop science TV show moderated by [[Naoki Matayoshi]].<ref>{{cite web|title=千葉逸人先生、鈴木咲衣先生出演「又吉直樹のヘウレーカ！」今夜0時30分再放送|periodical=|publisher=日本評論社|url=https://www.nippyo.co.jp/topics/%E5%8D%83%E8%91%89%E9%80%B8%E4%BA%BA%E5%85%88%E7%94%9F%E3%80%81%E9%88%B4%E6%9C%A8%E5%92%B2%E8%A1%A3%E5%85%88%E7%94%9F%E5%87%BA%E6%BC%94%E3%80%8C%E5%8F%88%E5%90%89%E7%9B%B4%E6%A8%B9%E3%81%AE%E3%83%98/|url-status=|format=|access-date=2022-08-30|archive-url=|archive-date=|last=|date=|year=|language=|pages=|quote=}}</ref>

Following this, in 2019, he followed a call to [[Tōhoku University]], where he is currently working as a professor of mathematics <ref>{{Cite web |last=千葉逸人 [@HayatoChiba] |title=今年度で九州大学を退職し、４月から東北大学に教授として赴任することになりました。福岡では同僚も学生も飲み友達にもに恵まれて、すごく楽しい毎日でした。離れるのつらいです。みんなありがとう。仙台のみなさま、よろしくです。送別会と歓迎会と特に意味のない飲み会は無限に受け付けております！ |url=https://x.com/HayatoChiba/status/1068849257568886784 |access-date=2026-08-28 |website=Twitter}}</ref>
